items.title: Jim Cramer: Anthropic’s “Next $100 Billion in Revenue” Might Be Cybersecurity. CrowdStrike Should Worry
items.summary: Key TakeawaysDays before Anthropic’s IPO, Jim Cramer named cybersecurity as a possible source of the AI lab’s next $100 billion in revenue, given how good Claude is at spotting code vulnerabilities. A bigger Claude security push would make Anthropic a direct competitor to CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks, which both jumped nearly 3% early on Nov.

items.title: Palo Alto Networks Sank Nearly 10% in a Day. Arora Still Sees AI as “Durable Tailwinds”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysPalo Alto Networks reports fiscal first-quarter results on November 18, after a software selloff sent its shares down nearly 10% on November 5. Fortinet’s product revenue growth slowed to 37% from 52%, while Palo Alto’s product revenue grew 28.

items.title: CrowdStrike Doubles Down on AI Agents With $495 Million in Deals After a Record $333 Million ARR Quarter
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCrowdStrike agreed to buy Fiddler AI and Dreadnode, two AI agent security startups, for about $495 million, The Wall Street Journal reported. Net new ARR hit a record $333 million last quarter, up 51%, and CEO George Kurtz called it “the best quarter in CrowdStrike’s history.
